questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: -The angle of elevation of the top of a TV tower from three points $A, B$ and $C$ in a straight line through the foot of the tower are $\alpha, 2 \alpha$ and $3 \alpha$ respectively. If $A B=a$, then height of the tower is
questions.solution: Let $D E$ be the height of the tower. Now, in $\triangle A B E$, \begin{aligned} \angle A E B &=\angle E B C-\angle E A B \\ &=2 \alpha-\alpha=\alpha \\ \therefore \quad \angle A E B &=\angle B A E \\ \Rightarrow \quad B E &=A B=a \end{aligned} Now, $\angle E C B=180^{\circ}-\angle D C E=180-3 \alpha$ Now, in $\triangle B E C, \frac{B E}{\sin (180-3 \alpha)}=\frac{C E}{\sin 2 \alpha}$ [using sine rule] \begin{array}{ll} \Rightarrow & \frac{a}{\sin 3 \alpha}=\frac{C E}{\sin 2 \alpha} \\ \Rightarrow \quad & C E=\frac{a \sin 2 \alpha}{\sin 3 \alpha} \end{array} In $\triangle E D C$, \begin{aligned} \sin 3 \alpha &=\frac{D E}{C E} \\ \Rightarrow \quad D E &=C E \sin 3 \alpha \\ &=\frac{a \sin 2 \alpha}{\sin 3 \alpha} \times \sin 3 \alpha=a \sin 2 \alpha \end{aligned} Hence, height of tower is $a \sin 2 \alpha$.

questions.q: From an aeroplane flying, vertically above a horizontal road, the angles of depression of two consecutive stones on the same side of the aeroplane are observed to be $30^{\circ}$ and $60^{\circ}$ respectively. The height at which the aeroplane is flying in $\mathrm{km}$, is
questions.solution:
Let the distance of two consecutive stones are $(x, x+1)$. In $\triangle B C D$, we have

$\tan 60^{\circ}=\frac{h}{x}\Rightarrow \quad x=\frac{h}{\sqrt{3}}...(i)$ In $\triangle A B C$, we have $\tan 30^{\circ}=\frac{h}{x+1}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}=\frac{h}{x+1}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{h}{\sqrt{3}}+1=\sqrt{3 h}$ [by Eq. (i)] $\begin{array}{ll}\Rightarrow & h\left(\sqrt{3}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)=1 \\ \Rightarrow & h \cdot\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\right)=1 \Rightarrow h=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\end{array}$
